abbreviations.location: 006 Notation equivalence annotation; form remains uncertain

notes: **Statement 006-N1.** The opening completes the finite-type reconstruction conditions: bounded closed parts are of finite type, and compatibility is hereditary under the order. At 3 tests compatibility on strata; At 4 tests refinement on strata. At 5 relates refinement to inclusion for compatible multistrates; At 7 states transitivity of internal refinement. The bottom translates At 0–3 into M and a family of subsets (Grothendieck, 1986, scan 6). These general claims are background here; no representation theorem or global equivalence is certified.

**Statement 006-N2 — S row SA21-K7-01, targeted check.** The displayed At 6 literally assumes X◁F and explicitly glosses this as X∈F-tilde. Consequently X belongs to F^X by reflexivity and At 0. Every Y in F^X shares the upper figure F with X, so X and Y are compatible. At 5 then converts X≪Y to X≤Y. Thus X itself is the least member. M and all three readers independently checked this narrowly delimited redundancy claim. S’s literal report and this mathematical concern are confirmed. Its proposed X≪F is an emendation, not the scanned sign, and is not substituted.

**Limit of the S decision at this page gate.** Replacing only the triangular relation removes the written incidence guarantee that X is a multistratum; the displayed quantification otherwise names X,F in the figure set. The complete intended corrected domain and hypothesis are not established on this page. Scan 007, cited by S, was not opened before completing this gate; any later comparison is to be recorded as later evidence.

**Statement 006-N3 — local mismatch checked.** The Notation block literally names X as the least element of Y-tilde superscript x. Under the natural selected-family reading, its following i.e. condition instead requires every candidate to equal Y. A two-element chain a<b, with refinement equal to inclusion and X=a,Y=b, has selected family {a,b}: X is least, but the candidate a violates the displayed equality to Y. This refutes that local equivalence under the stated interpretation. R2 supplied this counterexample in its independent report; M rechecked it. The transcription retains X.

**Statement 006-N4 — conditional refined statement.** If the least-element phrase names Y, and the selected family means {Z◁Y : X≪Z}, the subsequent condition is equivalent: each candidate Z is ≤Y; if Y is also least, antisymmetry gives Z=Y. Conversely the displayed X≪Y and universal equality make the family {Y}. This check concerns that conditional local correction only, not an assertion that the author intended it or that the whole theory is consistent.

**Ink versus apparent layout.** A purported small arrow near the corollary is the A of adjacent At 4, as the unrotated contextual crop shows. Similarly the curve above the detached figures belongs to the opening “(ou X∈Omb(Y)…” line, not a closing parenthesis for the marginal criterion. Neither false addition is retained. The criterion has no separately legible de before figures; the large apparent connector is Si from the horizontal At 5 line. The detached short curve/dash above Axiome de and the genuine curved arrow are drawn separately.

**Literal irregularities and qualifications.** The initial and concluding At3 G do not settle the open C|G beneath the intervening tilde. At4 retains low c|G; At6’s ∀ state and the ∃ before réunion have explicit state alternatives. The margin begins G,H but its formula uses F,G. AtM2 has literal <. At7 has a filled middle superscript, two open neighbours and two tiny doubtful colon-like marks before Z. The first auxiliary Phi prime is clear; the repeated prime may be a descender from que above. Figures de t.f., boundedness, compatibility and the indicated domains remain the manuscript’s qualifications. No new date/title or explicit verification request is present.

**Later comparison after scan007.** The newly read live AtM4(a) explicitly has Si X≪Y. This supports S’s refinement-based intent conjecture textually, while its revised wording and stratum-level domain prevent treating it as an exact proof of the proposed X≪F emendation. The scan006 transcription remains unchanged; see 007-N2.
